info.name: Qeet ID - API
info.description:
Complete request collection for the qeet-id backend (Go monolith).

## Setup

1. Start the backend: `cd backend && make run` (defaults to `http://localhost:4001`).
2. Import this collection AND the companion environment (`qeet-id.postman_environment.json`).
3. Select the **qeet-id (local)** environment in the Postman environment dropdown.
4. **First time / fresh DB:** run **03 Auth → 01 Signup**. It creates a **tenant-less** user and signs them in, auto-populating `{{userId}}`, `{{accessToken}}` and `{{refreshToken}}` (no tenant yet). Then run **09 Tenants → 02 Create tenant** to create a tenant and become its owner — that populates `{{tenantId}}`.
5. **Returning users:** run **03 Auth → 02 Login** with the saved tenant_id + email + password.

## Journey Map

Folders are numbered in onboarding order:

- **01–02** Start here
- **03–06** Human authentication
- **07–08** MFA & step-up
- **09–14** Accounts & tenancy
- **15–18** Authorization
- **19–21** Non-human / programmatic identity
- **22–25** OAuth / OIDC provider
- **26–30** Federation / enterprise SSO
- **31–33** Extensibility & events
- **34–42** Tenant configuration & security
- **43–47** Governance & compliance
- **48–50** Insights
- **51–52** Advanced product capabilities
- **53** Commercial
- **54** Platform internals

## Conventions

- All authed requests inherit a `Bearer {{accessToken}}` header from the collection root.
- IDs (`{{tenantId}}`, `{{userId}}`, `{{roleId}}`, …) are written back to collection variables by the corresponding `Create` / `Signup` requests, so you can chain them.
- Routes prefixed `/v1/...` are versioned API surface. Discovery / JWKS live at root (`/.well-known/...`) per the OIDC spec.

exec: throw new Error('baseUrl is not set. Select the qeet-id (local) environment or override --env-var baseUrl=...');
// The backend CSRF middleware (httpx/csrf.go) requires non-Bearer mutation
// requests to carry (a) an allow-listed Origin/Referer and (b) a double-
// submit cookie pair (qe_csrf + X-CSRF-Token). Bearer-token traffic skips
// entirely. Postman is not a browser so it sends neither header — handle
// it transparently here so the public auth routes (signup/login/recovery/
// invite-accept/oauth-token) work out of the box.
// If we already have a cached CSRF token from a prior seed, just echo it.
// Otherwise, seed the cookie by GETting /healthz and extract qe_csrf
// from Set-Cookie. Postman will wait for this async call before firing
pm.sendRequest({ url: baseUrl + '/healthz', method: 'GET' }, function (err, res) {
// Skip everything if the request errored out (no response, e.g. connection refused).
// Universal sanity checks. Per-request tests still run.
// Safety-net token capture: if any response carries access_token / refresh_token,
// keep collection vars in sync. Per-request tests still own the primary capture.
} catch (e) { /* non-JSON or empty body — ignore */ }

request.description:
Public self-service signup. Takes only `{email, password, display_name?}`. In ONE transaction the backend:

1. Generates a personal tenant for the new user (slug like `personal-<12hex>`, name like `"Jane's workspace"`).
2. Creates the user with a password credential.
3. Creates a system `owner` role for the personal tenant and grants it every platform permission.
4. Assigns the user to that owner role.
5. Issues an access + refresh token pair (auto-login).

The user can rename their workspace or create more from `Tenants → New tenant`.

**Email is globally unique** — same address can't sign up twice across the platform.

**Errors:**
- 409 — email already in use
- 422 — validation failed (password < 8 chars, invalid email, …)
Hosted-login end-user self-registration into an existing tenant (B2C).
Hosted-login: verifies credentials and sets the HttpOnly SSO cookie (qe_ls). Postman stores the cookie in its jar for subsequent /v1/oauth/authorize calls.
Hosted-login: finish a two-step login and set the SSO cookie.
Hosted-login logout: revoke the SSO session and clear the qe_ls cookie.

Public (no bearer) — bootstraps a brand-new tenant-less account on a passkey (passwordless counterpart to POST /auth/signup; no password is created). Runnable as-is: returns a WebAuthn CredentialCreation challenge (`session_id` + `publicKey`). Enumeration-safe (250ms timing floor + neutral 422 on conflict). Handler: internal/access/passkeys/passkey.go signupBegin.

exec: try { const b = pm.response.json(); if (b.session_id) pm.collectionVariables.set('passkeySignupSessionId', b.session_id); } catch(e){}

request.description: [setup] Public, but NOT runnable from Postman alone. `credential` must be a REAL WebAuthn attestation produced by an authenticator (hardware security key, a platform authenticator, or a VIRTUAL authenticator — e.g. Chrome DevTools 'WebAuthn' tab or a WebAuthn test harness) in response to the `publicKey` challenge returned by the begin call. The `{}` placeholder here will 422 ('invalid attestation'). On success returns 201 with a token pair (access_token/refresh_token/user_id/session_id) — captured below. Handler: passkey.go signupFinish → FinishSignup.

Public — tenant-scoped hosted self-registration (passwordless counterpart to POST /auth/register). TENANT HINT: the target tenant is passed in the JSON body as `tenant_id` ({{tenantId}}); there is no query-param variant — the handler reads `tenant_id` from the body only and 400s if it's missing. Gated by the tenant's `self_registration_enabled` policy (403 if disabled). Runnable when self-registration is on: returns `session_id` + `publicKey` challenge. Handler: passkey.go tenantSignupBegin → BeginTenantSignup.

request.description: Migration tooling for teams leaving another IdP. The request body is that vendor's own raw user-export file, converted to the same shape POST /v1/users/bulk accepts and run through the identical per-row partial-success pipeline. The example body is a synthetic 2-line Auth0 NDJSON export (Content-Type application/x-ndjson); for cognito use text/csv, for azure_b2c application/json. No vendor exports a portable password hash, so every imported row lands with no password credential (passkey / magic link / OTP / admin reset are how they first sign in). Response: { succeeded, failed, errors[] }. Admin-gated on user.write. Swap the body for a real export file to migrate production users.

request.description: Deletes the tenant's registered provider config by its `provider` name key. 404 if it was never registered.

PUBLIC (no bearer). The fixed OAuth2 redirect_uri registered with the third-party provider — mounted in the router's public group (TokenVault.MountPublic). It is driven by the BROWSER redirect after the user consents at the provider: the provider appends `?state=&code=` and the handler exchanges the code, encrypts the tokens, and renders a minimal HTML confirmation page (never a redirect). Cannot be exercised directly from Postman — the `state` is single-use and minted by the connect ceremony, and the `code` comes from a real IdP. Marked [setup]. Without a valid state/code it returns a 400 HTML error page.

Authed (uses the caller's own tenant + user from the JWT). Starts an OAuth2 authorization-code ceremony against the tenant's registered provider config and returns JSON `{ "authorize_url": "..." }` with 200 — NOT a 302 redirect. The client is expected to send the user's browser to that URL; the provider then redirects back to /v1/vault/tokens/callback. Marked [setup] because it requires the provider to be registered first (404 otherwise) and only completes end-to-end against a real IdP.

The "agent-safe" fetch: returns `{ "access_token": "..." }`, transparently refreshing if expired; the refresh token is never exposed. Marked [setup] because it needs (1) the provider registered, (2) a connected account for the caller's userID (real OAuth ceremony completed), and (3) a PRINCIPAL/agent token carrying `vault:<provider>` or `vault:read` scope — a plain user access token lacks that scope and gets 403. Every access is audited (vault.tokens.accessed). To exercise: mint an agent token with a vault scope and swap the Authorization header to that token.
Deletes the calling user's connected account (token grant) for this provider. 404 if there is no connected account.

Returns rollup metrics for the admin dashboard: total users, MAU, signups vs prior period, signins, failure rates, weekly activity (last 8 weeks).

Cursor-paginated activity feed derived from the tenant's audit log (`{ events: [...], next_cursor? }`). Tenant comes from the JWT principal only. Gated by `audit.read`. `limit` 1–200 (handler default 50); severity/category are derived and applied post-fetch; `q` is a websearch_to_tsquery expression.

[setup] SERVER-SENT EVENTS. Implemented and gated by `audit.read`, but this is a long-lived text/event-stream connection: the server extends the write deadline to 1 hour and emits `event: activity` frames plus `: keep-alive` comments. Postman's request runner will hold the connection open and not complete like a normal request — open it in the SSE/streaming view or via curl. Optional `Last-Event-ID` header triggers replay of missed events. Filters (types/severity/category) apply to both replay and live stream.

Tenant-scoped fuzzy search across user, organization, group, role, oidc_client, and audit_event. `q` is REQUIRED (1+ chars after trimming; 400 otherwise). Each resource type is gated behind its own read permission — types the caller cannot read are silently excluded. Returns `{ results: [...], next_cursor? }`. `limit` 1–50 (default 20).

Returns whether the AI qeetai is configured server-side (`{ configured, provider, model }`). Never returns key material. `configured` is true only when QEETAI_PROVIDER + QEETAI_API_KEY are set; when false, conversation CRUD still works but the messages stream returns 409.
Lists the authenticated user's qeetai conversations (tenant + user scoped), pinned-first then most-recently-updated. Returns `{ items: Conversation[] }`.

exec: try { const r = pm.response.json(); const arr = r.items || r; if (Array.isArray(arr) && arr.length && arr[0].id !== undefined) pm.collectionVariables.set('qeetaiConversationId', arr[0].id); } catch(e){}

request.description: Creates a new qeetai conversation thread for the authenticated user. Body is optional (title defaults to "New conversation" server-side). Returns the created Conversation; its id is captured into {{qeetaiConversationId}}.

exec: try { const b = pm.response.json(); if (b.id) pm.collectionVariables.set('qeetaiConversationId', b.id); } catch(e){}

request.description: Returns a conversation with its full message history (`{ conversation, messages }`). Scoped by tenant AND user — a conversation owned by another user returns 404.
Renames and/or pins-unpins a conversation. Both `title` and `pinned` are optional (nullable) — send only the fields you want to change. Returns the updated Conversation.
Deletes a conversation and all its messages (cascade). 404 if out of scope. Run this AFTER the get/patch/messages tests for {{qeetaiConversationId}}.

Opens a streaming turn of the conversation, emitting the model's response as Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream). Body: `{ message }` (and/or `tool_results`, `context`). The qeetai never mutates domain state itself — tool calls are streamed as SSE events for the browser to execute under the user's own token. Marked [setup] because it requires the qeetai to be CONFIGURED (QEETAI_PROVIDER + QEETAI_API_KEY / an LLM key) — otherwise it returns 409 qeetai_unconfigured. Postman does not render SSE incrementally; expect the raw event stream in the response body.
Issue a W3C JWT-VC. Returns {id, credential} — credential is the signed JWT-VC.
Public: any relying party can verify a presented JWT-VC. Returns validity + revocation.
Begin a paid plan change via hosted Stripe/Razorpay checkout. Requires the provider env keys to be configured server-side.
Provider webhook (path is the provider: stripe | razorpay). Signature-verified server-side — Postman calls will be rejected without a valid provider signature.

Dev-only mock hosted-checkout PAGE (returns HTML), public/no-auth. Route exists in the router but is intentionally undocumented in the OpenAPI spec. 404 unless the sandbox provider is enabled (PAYMENT_SANDBOX_BASE_URL). `ref` comes from a real 'Start checkout' whose `checkout_url` points here; `success_url`/`cancel_url` are open-redirect validated. `[setup]` — meant to be opened in a browser, not asserted in Newman.

Dev-only sandbox 'pay' action (form-urlencoded), public/no-auth — undocumented in the OpenAPI spec but registered by the router. Completes the checkout referenced by `ref` (same path a real provider webhook takes) then 303-redirects to `success_url`. 404 unless the sandbox is enabled. `[setup]` — needs a valid `ref` from a started checkout.
Inspects dead-lettered outbox events for ops triage. Requires platform-admin gating in the deployment.
